operands: every product operand an integer with |a| <= 2^15 - 1 = 32767

routes.f64: one float64 product; exact while n (2^15 - 1)^2 < 2^53, n below 2^23
routes.f32: a = 256 a1 + a0, a0 in [-128, 127], a1 in [-128, 128]; four float32 products in chunks of 1,024 inputs; |partial sums| <= 1024 x 2^14 = 2^24. The digits need 8 significant bits, so they are exact as TF32 (11) and bfloat16 (8) inputs too, with float32 accumulation
routes.i8: u = a + 2^15 in [1, 2^16 - 1], u = 256 u1 + u0, u1 and u0 in [0, 255] (uint8), the same for b; four int32 MatMulInteger products of uint8 by uint8; partial sums <= n 255^2 < 2^31, n <= 33,025; then a b = u_a u_b - 2^15 (row sums of a + column sums of b) - n 2^30 in int64

kernel_intermediate.why exact: every product and every partial sum is an integer below 2^53, and every integer below 2^53 is a float64; a sum or a fused a b + c whose exact value is a float64 is returned exactly

kernel_intermediate.largest partial sum, any order or groupi: 1,024 x 128 x 128 = 2^24 within a chunk; the chunks are added in int64
kernel_intermediate.why exact: every digit product is an integer of magnitude at most 2^14 and every partial sum of a chunk, in any order, is an integer of magnitude at most 2^24; every integer of magnitude at most 2^24 is a float32, so no addition or fused multiply-add rounds. The digits have at most 8 significant bits (|d| <= 128), so they are also exact as TF32 or bfloat16 inputs

one uint8 by uint8 product (up to 65,025) does not fit a signed 16-bit lane, so a uint8 by uint8 kernel has to widen before it adds: a pair needs 18 bits, any sum of k products is at most k 255^2 < 2^31 for k <= 33,025. routes_test.py's 'all +max' puts every pair at 130,050 and fails on a kernel that keeps less. uint8 by uint8 is the MatMulInteger type pair every onnxruntime version implements
kernel_intermediate.the digits it replaces: a1 = a >> 8 (int8), a0 = a & 255 (uint8): a uint8 by int8 kernel without VNNI adds adjacent pairs in int16 with saturation, and 2 x 255 x 128 = 65,280 > 32,767; a 7-bit unsigned digit (2 x 127 x 128 = 32,512) would hold, at six products instead of four. onnxruntime 1.23.2 (macOS x86-64) could not build a MatMulInteger session for one of the pairs with an int8 operand (NOT_IMPLEMENTED)

residual: clamp plus one linear output
rope: q or k (a linear output) times cos, two terms
scores: q16 . k16 shifted by sh_q + sh_k (<= 10 + 10), at 2^-32
peel key: |x| 2^11 + index, |x| within the largest clamp
i8 route: sum of u_a u_b, u = a + 2^15 <= 2^16 - 1, over the widest product (n = 1536)
i8 route: 2^15 (row sum of a + column sum of b) + n 2^30
